---
title: "Bed level per cell, after the last MeshKernel rebuild"
---

In a model built with hydrolib / D-HyDAMO the bed level goes in per cell, as
`mesh2d_face_z` in the model's net file with `bedLevType = 1`, on exactly the cells
MeshKernel builds from the nodes and edges: after the last change to the mesh the cells
are rebuilt with MeshKernel once more, the bed level is given to those cells, and the
mesh is not changed afterwards. No sample file (`bodem_2d.xyz`) is needed.

The D-HYDRO GUI, like hydrolib's `mesh2d_from_netcdf`, builds the cells again from nodes
and edges, and MeshKernel also makes a cell of a small hole. A level per cell fits only
when the net file holds those cells, in that order.

Found on the Geul model (D-HYDRO Suite 2026.02):

- Model 8d (2026-11-12): the net file lacked one cell that MeshKernel builds (a hole
  left by a clip); the GUI rejected `mesh2d_face_z` ("number of values is not equal to
  multiple of all argument values"). A sample file with two `[Initial] bedlevel` blocks
  worked around it (the route this documentation first gave, ADR-0003).
- Berekening_10rq (2026-11-25): refined-quads → `mesh2d_from_netcdf` → branch clip →
  bed level. A fresh MeshKernel rebuild of the saved net file gave 277,208 cells, the
  file 277,207: the branch clip had left a hole after the rebuild.
- Berekening_10rq2: the same with one more MeshKernel rebuild right before the bed
  level. A fresh rebuild of the saved net file gives the same 277,208 cells in the same
  order, and the model loads in the GUI with the right bed levels.

This is the route of the D-HyDAMO example notebook (HYDROLIB PR #263, `use_refined_quads`).

MeshKernel does not keep cells but nodes and edges, and builds the cells again each time:
a small hole becomes a cell (cells "appear"), a cell a clip removed can come back, and a
ring it does not take for a cell (more than six nodes) is not a cell after the rebuild
(cells "disappear"); see [ADR-0004](0004-no-holes-meshkernel-closes.qmd). The model
therefore holds the cells of the last rebuild, which can differ from the mesh
refined-quads made.

## Considered Options

- **Bed level as samples (`bodem_2d.xyz`, two `[Initial]` blocks, `mesh2d_face_z`
  removed after saving).** Works, but needs an extra file, field file blocks and a
  post-processing step on the saved net file. Replaced for now; it can come back as an
  alternative for a user to whom cells appearing or disappearing through MeshKernel is a
  problem, since samples are assigned by location, not per cell.
- **Remove the cells MeshKernel adds (gap repair).** Rejected: the GUI adds them again.

## Consequences

- The documentation (Use the mesh in D-HYDRO) gives this route and a check: read the
  saved net file again with hydrolib; the cells must be the same, in the same order.
- A clip after the last rebuild breaks the rule. A single cell a clip removes comes back
  in the rebuild, as it does in the GUI.
- The cells depend on the MeshKernel that builds them; if the GUI's MeshKernel ever
  builds other cells, the check above does not show it. Opening the model in the GUI
  remains the final test.
